title: Align per-direction IO pricing with enterprise security questionnaire commitments — simulations & contract language
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Sales and legal report repeated questions from enterprise security questionnaires (SQ) about how billed usage maps to customer obligations in contracts. Customers negotiating minimums and audit clauses ask how streaming tokens vs non-stream tokens and ingress/egress (input vs output) are metered, and whether SQ responses implying guaranteed unit economics create hidden revenue exposure for Redwood. Goal: design a pricing experiment & candidate contract language that reconciles per-direction IO metering, streaming behavior, and minimum commitments so sales can confidently propose terms without exposing undue risk.
background: Recent enterprise deals in EMEA flagged two concerns: (1) security questionnaires require explicit examples of billing for live streaming sessions (developers expect constant small output chunks), and (2) procurement teams want minimum spend floors that are 'consumption equivalent' across interactive (streaming chat) and batch API usage. Current hosted API meters input/output tokens and treats streaming as identical to synchronous generation for billing, but sales has had to add manual clarifications in contracts. We need an experiment that quantifies revenue variance under candidate rules and surfaced contract language that standardizes commitments.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation model that forecasts revenue delta across top-50 enterprise workloads under three metering proposals (current symmetric I/O, output-weighted, streaming-adjusted)
Draft contract clause templates (consumer-friendly + enterprise-negotiation variant) that explain metering rules for SQ responses
A/B experiment plan for a 4-week field trial with opt-in enterprise customers and a rollback plan
Security review sign-off and legal-approved FAQ for sales and CSM teams
Clear recommendation (go / iterate / cancel) with estimated revenue and risk impact
updates: 2025-02-11 — Kickoff: met with Legal (Sara Kim) and Sales Ops (Jordan Lee) to capture constraints from enterprise contracts and SQ templates. Legal requires explicit definition of 'streaming event' in contracts.
2025-02-12 — Data request sent to Eng metrics team (ENG-23841) for per-customer per-route token breakdown and streaming session heuristics for last 6 months. Initial ETA 2025-02-17.

2025-02-14 — Ran small internal simulation using synthetic workload mix: chat-heavy (60% output), embeddings-heavy (95% input), and RAG ingestion patterns. Early result: output-weighted pricing increases billed tokens by ~18% for chat-first customers, reduces by ~6% for ingestion-first customers.

2025-02-16 — Legal flagged risk: customers could request reassessment clause tied to SQ statements; proposed contract language adds an audit window and sample workload statements to bound accounting method.
2025-02-17 — Security review: InfoSec requested an explicit statement that billing rules do not change access controls or data retention. Security review in progress; assigned to Priya Malhotra.

2025-02-18 — Decision workshop: narrowed to two candidate metering proposals for field trial: (A) Output-weighted default with streaming microburst normalization, (B) Symmetric I/O but streaming sessions billed at 0.9x output to recognize small-chunk overhead. Marcelo to prepare simulation results for exec review on 2025-02-20.
tradeoffs_and_notes: Output-weighted simplifies sales narrative (customers pay for what they receive) but risks revenue leakage on ingestion-heavy analytics customers and will be pushed back by partners using embeddings at scale.
Streaming microburst normalization prevents inflated bills from many tiny chunks but adds implementation complexity in the billing pipeline and requires Eng acceptance (ENG-23841 + ENG-24012).
Legal prefers deterministic, auditable rules over heuristics; any heuristic (eg. sessionbased normalization) must be documented with example calculations for SQ responses.

We must avoid contract language that can be interpreted as a guaranteed unit price over time; prefer language that defines calculation method and preserves Redwood's right to change billing with notice and migration credits.

Eng to provide per-session streaming heuristics and implementation cost estimate by 2025-02-24 (ENG-24012 created)
Legal to draft two contract clause templates and an SQ-friendly appendix by 2025-02-25
Prepare customer-facing FAQ and one-pager for sales and CSM once a candidate is chosen
Run 4-week opt-in field trial with 8 enterprise customers starting 2025-03-10 if exec approves
